text:
Maya: Heads-up — since ~1724999000 we're seeing a surge of node-provision failures in eu-west when launching gpu pools. Errors point to KMS decrypt denies + egress blocked to our proxy.
Maya: Sample from node bootstrap: ```2024-05-02T14:12:03Z error: KMS.DecryptDenied: access denied for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/abcd
2024-05-02T14:12:04Z warn: connection to proxy.example.net:443: write tcp 10.10.5.12:34567->34.56.78.90:443: write: connection refused
```
Maya: Also seeing NAT/firewall logs showing `DENY` for 10.10.0.0/16 -> 0.0.0.0/0 from the new egress ACL change.
Jeff: Oh — that change went out in firewall-managed this morning. I just pinged network-eng. @Li can you confirm if our privatesubnet CIDR or route table was rotated in the rollout?
Li: Yup, firewall team replaced a permissive rule with a strict egress ACL that only allows 10.20.0.0/16 -> allowed endpoints. Our GPU warm pool instances are coming up in older AZs with 10.10.0.0/16 so they get dropped.
Li: Quick workaround: added temporary SG egress rule to allow 0.0.0.0/0 for the warmpool tag. Command I ran: ```aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0warmpool --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0``` — will monitor.
Samir: That SG workaround unblocks bootstrap but KMS decrypt denies still need fix — looks like the key policy was tightened to deny cross-account decrypts for nodes with older role ARN. The keystore change was part of last night's compliance rollout.
Samir: Error from KMS logs: `PrincipalNotAuthorizedException principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/gpu-bootstrap-role not allowed to decrypt`.
Maya: So two independent failures: egress ACL + KMS policy. Rolling SG is fine short-term but we need an audit-friendly fix.
Eva: For prod-critical pools we should avoid cross-region fallback to save egress cost and data exposure. If eu-west can't provision we should failover to dedicated eu-central reserved capacity rather than spin up in us-east and pay cross-region egress.
Jeff: Agreed. I'll message capacity-team to pin canaries to eu-central reserved nodes while we fix keystore/policies. That avoids surprise billing for cross-region traffic.
ops-bot: ALERT: node-provision-failure (eu-west) spike: +38 failures in last 10m. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20240502-54
Li: Action plan: 1) rollback egress ACL change for the affected subnets (networking) — Jeff to coordinate. 2) add temporary key policy exception for gpu-bootstrap-role with strict condition on source VPC (security) — Samir. 3) mark warmpool instances as exempt and requeue provisioning (infra) — Maya. 4) review cost impact if any cross-region warmups were triggered (finance/ops) — Eva.
Samir: Proposed minimal KMS policy snippet to add for emergency: ```"Principal": {"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456:role/gpu-bootstrap-role"}, "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:sourceVpc":"vpc-0123abcd"}}``` — will open PR and request an expedited review.
Jeff: I'm on a call with networking now. If rollback is approved I'll post here the rollback window. ETA 15-20m.
Maya: Monitoring: provisioner queue length dropping after SG patch, but KMS errors remain at ~20% of attempts.
Eva: Noted — if the KMS update needs >1h I'll spin up reserved eu-central extra nodes and update routing to prefer them; will report cost delta in channel.
Li: After Samir's PR merges, we should rotate the affected bootstrap tokens and capture audit events for compliance. Don't want lingering exceptions.
Maya: Assignments: Jeff (network rollback), Samir (KMS PR & audit note), Li (rotate tokens + validate warmpool), Eva (cost/backup capacity), Maya (monitor & requeue). Check back in 30.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: rollback approved by netops at 1725000200; firewall change reverted for 10.10.0.0/16 subnets.
Jeff: rollback applied. provisioning success rate back to normal in eu-west. Samir — any update on PR?
Samir: PR opened: https://git.redwood/security/pulls/482 — added sourceVpc condition and audit logging. Requested expedited review.
Maya: Great. Closing loop: once PR merges Li please run the token rotation script: ```scripts/rotate-bootstrap-tokens.sh --env=eu-west --tag=warmpool``` and post result.
Li: Will do. Rotation scheduled at 1725000600.
Eva: I'll post a short cost note after rotation completes. Current rough estimate for temporary reserved capacity = +$1.2k/day if we keep pinned nodes for 24h.
Maya: Thanks all. Leaving thread open for the audit log handoff. :thumbsup:
